Q2 FY2026 quarter-end: signed long-term custom AI accelerator contract; remaining performance obligations ~$164.6B
Proxy cites FY2025 record revenue $63.9B, operating cash $27.5B, free cash flow $26.9B driven by AI semiconductors and VMware software
Entered $7.5B five-year unsecured revolving credit facility (2025 Credit Agreement)
Registered new senior notes offering (424B5) to manage debt stack
Filed FY2025 10-K: revenue $63.9B (+24%), semiconductor $36.9B (+22%), infrastructure software $27.0B (+26%), operating cash flow $27.5B
Registered senior notes offering (424B5) amid VMware integration and AI silicon ramp
Registered senior notes offering (424B5) to fund operations and capital return
Filed FY2024 10-K: first full fiscal year with VMware; revenue $51.6B, debt ~$66.3B
Closed VMware acquisition for ~$30.8B cash plus 544M Broadcom shares (~$53.4B stock value); added infrastructure software segment
Charlie Kawwas appointed President, Semiconductor Solutions Group; leads AI and networking silicon portfolio
Completed acquisition of CA Technologies, expanding enterprise software footprint before VMware
Avago Technologies acquired legacy Broadcom, forming today's Broadcom Inc. platform

industry.structure: Broadcom spans merchant and custom semiconductors (networking, storage, broadband, wireless, AI XPUs) and infrastructure software (VMware private cloud, mainframe, cybersecurity, FC SAN). Oligopolistic niches in switching and enterprise software sit alongside cyclical AI silicon demand and heavy acquisition-driven goodwill.
industry.share_shift: Semiconductor solutions revenue rose 22% to $36.9B in FY2025 on AI networking and custom accelerator demand; infrastructure software rose 26% to $27.0B as VMware subscriptions scaled. Remaining performance obligations reached ~$164.6B by Q2 FY2026 with a new custom AI accelerator contract.
industry.trend: AI data-center build-outs drive custom silicon and networking content; VMware subscription transition and upfront license recognition add revenue lumpiness. ~$62B debt stack and customer concentration (~40% top-five end customers) remain structural constraints on equity returns at premium multiples.
